title: KCET 2011 Chemistry
subject: chemistry
source: KEA question paper (copy) + KEA answer key column A1

questions.q: Which one of the following statements is FALSE?
options: During roasting, moisture is removed from the ore.
The ore is freed from almost all nonmetallic impurities.
Calcination of ore is carried out in the absence of any blast of air.
The concentrated zinc blende is subjected to calcination during its extraction by pyrometallurgy.
questions.chapter: Old syllabus: General Principles and Processes of Isolation of Elements
questions.explanation: Zinc blende (ZnS) is a sulphide ore and is subjected to roasting, not calcination; calcination is used for carbonate/hydrated oxide ores, so this statement is false.

questions.q: Which one of the following sets of quantum numbers represents the highest energy level in an atom?
questions.explanation: Using the (n+l) rule, option 3 (3d) has n+l=5, higher than 4s(4), 3p(4) and 3s(3), so it represents the highest energy level.

questions.q: When $O_2$ is converted into $O_2^+$; ..............
options: both paramagnetic character and bond order increase
paramagnetic character decreases and the bond order increases
questions.explanation: $O_2$ (bond order 2, 2 unpaired electrons) loses an electron to form $O_2^+$ (bond order 2.5, 1 unpaired electron), so paramagnetism decreases while bond order increases.

questions.q: In chromite ore, the oxidation number of iron and chromium are respectively ...........
questions.explanation: Chromite is FeO.Cr$_2$O$_3$ (FeCr$_2$O$_4$), in which iron is +2 and chromium is +3.

questions.q: The number of naturally occurring $p$-block elements that are diamagnetic is ..............
questions.explanation: The five stable naturally occurring noble gases (He, Ne, Ar, Kr, Xe) have completely filled shells and are diamagnetic.

questions.q: If the energies of the two photons are in the ratio of 3 : 2, their wavelengths will be in the ratio of .....................
questions.explanation: Since $E=\dfrac{hc}{\lambda}$, wavelength is inversely proportional to energy, so the wavelength ratio is the inverse of the energy ratio, i.e. 2 : 3.

questions.q: Which one of these is NOT TRUE for benzene?
options: There are three carbon-carbon single bonds and three carbon-carbon double bonds.
It forms only one type of monosubstituted product.
The bond angle between carbon-carbon bonds is 120$^0$.
Heat of hydrogenation of benzene is less than the theoretical value.
questions.explanation: All six C-C bonds in benzene are equivalent due to delocalization (bond length about 1.39 Å, between single and double bond lengths), so it does not literally have three single and three double bonds.

questions.q: Generally, the first ionization energy increases along a period. But there are some exceptions. The one which is NOT an exception is ..............
questions.explanation: Ionization energy increases normally from Na to Mg; Be-B, N-O and Mg-Al are all exceptions to the normal trend due to stable filled or half-filled subshells.

questions.q: Out of the given two compounds [A is 4-nitrophenol, with $OH$ and $NO_2$ para to each other; B is 2-nitrophenol, with $OH$ and $NO_2$ ortho to each other], the vapour pressure of B at a particular temperature is ..............
options: higher or lower than A depending on the size of the vessel
questions.explanation: In B (ortho-nitrophenol) intramolecular hydrogen bonding occurs, so it does not associate strongly and has a higher vapour pressure than A (para-nitrophenol), which has intermolecular hydrogen bonding.

questions.q: Increasing order of carbon-carbon bond length for the following is ...........  C$_2$H$_4$ (A), C$_2$H$_2$ (B), C$_6$H$_6$ (C), C$_2$H$_6$ (D)
questions.explanation: Bond length increases as bond order decreases: triple bond (C$_2$H$_2$) < double bond (C$_2$H$_4$) < aromatic bond (C$_6$H$_6$) < single bond (C$_2$H$_6$), giving B < A < C < D.

questions.q: A mixture of $CaCl_2$ and $NaCl$ weighing 4.44 g is treated with sodium carbonate solution to precipitate all the calcium ions as calcium carbonate. The calcium carbonate so obtained is heated strongly to get 0.56 g of $CaO$. The percentage of $NaCl$ in the mixture is .................. [Atomic mass of $Ca=40$].
questions.explanation: Moles $CaO$ = 0.56/56 = 0.01 mol = moles $Ca$; mass $CaCl_2$ = 0.01 × 111 = 1.11 g, so $NaCl$ = 4.44 − 1.11 = 3.33 g, which is 75% of the mixture.

questions.q: 50 cm$^3$ of 0.2 N $HCl$ is titrated against 0.1 N $NaOH$ solution. The titration was discontinued after adding 50 cm$^3$ of $NaOH$. The remaining titration is completed by adding 0.5 N $KOH$. The volume of $KOH$ required for completing the titration is ...........
questions.explanation: Milliequivalents of $HCl$ = 50×0.2 = 10; milliequivalents of $NaOH$ added = 50×0.1 = 5; the remaining 5 meq are neutralized by 0.5 N $KOH$, needing 5/0.5 = 10 cm$^3$.

questions.q: The rms velocity of hydrogen is $\sqrt{7}$ times the rms velocity of nitrogen. If $T$ is the temperature of the gas, which of the following is true?
questions.explanation: Since $u_{rms}\propto\sqrt{T/M}$ and $u_{H_2}=\sqrt7\\,u_{N_2}$, squaring and using $M_{H_2}=2$, $M_{N_2}=28$ gives $T_{N_2}=2T_{H_2}$.

questions.q: 25 g of each of the following gases are taken at 27$^0$C and 600 mm pressure. Which of these will have the least volume?
questions.explanation: At the same T and P, $V\propto n=\text{mass}/M$; $HI$ has the largest molar mass (128), giving the fewest moles and hence the least volume.

questions.q: The amount of heat evolved when 500 cm$^3$ of 0.1 M $HCl$ is mixed with 200 cm$^3$ of 0.2 M $NaOH$ is ..............
questions.explanation: Moles $NaOH$ (limiting reagent) = 0.2×0.2 = 0.04 mol; using the standard enthalpy of neutralization of a strong acid-strong base (≈57.3 kJ/mol), heat evolved = 0.04×57.3 = 2.292 kJ.

questions.q: The enthalpy of vaporization of benzene is +35.3 kJ/mol at its boiling point of 80$^0$C. The entropy change in the transition of vapour to liquid at its boiling point is .............. [in J mol$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$].
questions.explanation: $\Delta S=-\Delta H_{vap}/T=-35300/353\approx-100$ J mol$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$, since condensation is the reverse of vaporization.

questions.q: Based on the first law of thermodynamics, which one of the following is correct?
questions.explanation: Using $\Delta U=q+w$ (w = work done on the system): for a cyclic process $\Delta U=0$, so $q=-w$; the other three statements contradict the first law under this convention.

questions.q:
Consider the following gaseous equilibria with equilibrium constants $K_1$ and $K_2$ respectively.
$SO_{2(g)}+\dfrac{1}{2}O_{2(g)} \rightleftharpoons SO_{3(g)}$
$2SO_{3(g)} \rightleftharpoons 2SO_{2(g)}+O_{2(g)}$
The equilibrium constants are related as ..............
questions.explanation: The second equation is the reverse of the first, doubled, so $K_2=(1/K_1)^2=1/K_1^2$, i.e. $K_1^2=1/K_2$.

questions.q: During the adsorption of Krypton on activated charcoal at low temperature; ..............
questions.explanation: Adsorption is exothermic ($\Delta H<0$) and randomness decreases as gas molecules become confined to the solid surface ($\Delta S<0$).

questions.q: For the reversible reaction, $A_{(s)}+B_{(g)} \rightleftharpoons C_{(g)}+D_{(g)}$, $\Delta G^0=-350\\ kJ$, which one of the following statements is true?
options: Equilibrium constant is greater than one.
questions.explanation: A large negative $\Delta G^0$ gives $K=e^{-\Delta G^0/RT}\gg1$, so the equilibrium constant is much greater than one.

questions.q: Identify B and D in the following sequence of reactions: CH$_2$=CH$_2$ treated with conc. $H_2SO_4$ gives A; A on heating with $H_2O$ gives B; B treated with $PBr_3$ gives C; C treated with reagent D regenerates CH$_2$=CH$_2$.
questions.explanation: A is ethyl hydrogen sulphate; B is ethanol (hydrolysis of A); C is bromoethane (B + $PBr_3$); D is alcoholic $KOH$, which eliminates $HBr$ from C to regenerate ethylene.

questions.q: The compound which gives turbidity immediately with Lucas reagent at room temperature is ..............
questions.explanation: Tertiary alcohols react fastest with Lucas reagent (conc. $HCl$/$ZnCl_2$) via the $S_N1$ mechanism, giving immediate turbidity; 2-methylpropan-2-ol (tert-butanol) is the tertiary alcohol here.

questions.q: Ethyl benzene CANNOT be prepared by ..................
questions.explanation: The Wurtz reaction couples two alkyl halides and cannot attach an alkyl group to an aryl halide; Wurtz-Fittig, Friedel-Crafts alkylation and Clemmensen reduction (of acetophenone) can all give ethylbenzene.

questions.q: 1.2 g of organic compound on Kjeldahlization liberates ammonia which consumes 30 cm$^3$ of 1 N $HCl$. The percentage of nitrogen in the organic compound is ...........
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry: Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.explanation: %N $=\dfrac{1.4\times N\times V}{\text{mass}}=\dfrac{1.4\times1\times30}{1.2}=35$.

questions.q: Carbon cannot reduce $Fe_2O_3$ to $Fe$ at a temperature below 983 K because ...........
options: free energy change for the formation of $CO$ is more negative than that of $Fe_2O_3$
carbon has higher affinity towards oxygen than iron
iron has higher affinity towards oxygen than carbon
questions.chapter: Old syllabus: General Principles and Processes of Isolation of Elements
questions.explanation: On the Ellingham diagram, below 983 K the $\Delta G_f$ of iron oxide is more negative than that of carbon monoxide, i.e. iron has a higher affinity for oxygen than carbon at that temperature.

questions.q: The yellow precipitate formed during the chromyl chloride test is chemically .............
questions.explanation: $CrO_2Cl_2$ vapour is absorbed in $NaOH$ to give sodium chromate, which on treatment with acetic acid and lead acetate gives a yellow precipitate of lead chromate.

questions.q: One gram of silver gets distributed between 10 cm$^3$ of molten zinc and 100 cm$^3$ of molten lead at 800$^0$C. The percentage of silver still left in the lead layer is approximately ........
questions.chapter: Old syllabus: General Principles and Processes of Isolation of Elements
questions.explanation: With a Zn:Pb distribution ratio of about 300 (as in the Parkes desilverisation process), solving (1−x)/10 : x/100 = 300 gives x ≈ 0.032, i.e. about 3% of the silver remains in the lead layer.

questions.q: Which one of the following is true?
options: $NaOH$ is used in the concentration of bauxite ore.
$NaOH$ is a primary standard in volumetric analysis.
Manganous hydroxide is soluble in excess of $NaOH$ solution.
questions.chapter: Old syllabus: General Principles and Processes of Isolation of Elements
questions.explanation: In Bayer's process, bauxite is concentrated by dissolving $Al_2O_3$ in hot $NaOH$ as sodium aluminate; $NaOH$ is not a primary standard, $Mn(OH)_2$ is insoluble in excess $NaOH$, and $NaOH$ does react with $Cl_2$.

questions.q: In Ramsay and Rayleigh's isolation of noble gases from air, the nitrogen of the air is finally converted into ..................
questions.explanation: Repeated sparking of $N_2$ with excess $O_2$ over $NaOH$ solution converts atmospheric nitrogen into a mixture of sodium nitrite and sodium nitrate, leaving the inert gases behind.

questions.q: The spin only magnetic moment of $Fe^{2+}$ ion (in BM) is approximately ...........
questions.explanation: High-spin $Fe^{2+}$ ($d^6$) has 4 unpaired electrons; $\mu=\sqrt{n(n+2)}=\sqrt{4\times6}=\sqrt{24}\approx5$ BM.

questions.q: The IUPAC name of the complex $[Co(NH_3)_4Cl_2]Cl$ is ..............
questions.explanation: Ligands are named alphabetically (ammine before chloro); the counter ion $Cl^-$ balances a +1 complex ion charge, so cobalt is in the +3 state, giving tetraamminedichlorocobalt(III) chloride.

questions.q: Excess of silver nitrate solution is added to 100 ml of 0.01 M Pentaaqua chloro chromium (III) chloride solution. The mass of silver chloride obtained in grams is .............. [Atomic mass of silver is 108].
questions.explanation: $[Cr(H_2O)_5Cl]Cl_2$ has 2 ionizable $Cl^-$ per formula unit; moles complex = 0.1×0.01=$10^{-3}$, so moles ionizable $Cl^-$=$2\times10^{-3}$; mass $AgCl$=$2\times10^{-3}\times143.5=287\times10^{-3}$ g.

questions.q:
The following data were obtained during the first order decomposition of $2A_{(g)} \rightarrow B_{(g)}+C_{(s)}$ at a constant volume and at a particular temperature.
At the end of 10 min, total pressure = 300 Pascal.
After completion, total pressure = 200 Pascal.
The rate constant in min$^{-1}$ is ..............
questions.explanation: Since C is solid, total pressure $=P_0-p$ where $p$ is the pressure of B formed; at completion $P_0/2=200\Rightarrow P_0=400$ Pa, so at 10 min $P_A=200$ Pa; $k=\dfrac{2.303}{10}\log\dfrac{400}{200}=0.0693\\ min^{-1}$.

questions.q: The time required for 100% completion of a zero order reaction is ..............
questions.explanation: For a zero order reaction, $[A]=a-kt$; complete consumption occurs when $t=a/k$.

questions.q: The activation energy of a reaction at a given temperature is found to be 2.303 RT J mol$^{-1}$. The ratio of rate constant to the Arrhenius factor is ..............
pH value of which one of the following is NOT equal to one?
questions.explanation: $CH_3COOH$ is a weak acid and is not fully dissociated, so its pH is greater than 1; the other three all give $[H^+]=0.1$ M, i.e. pH=1.

questions.q: A buffer solution contains 0.1 mole of sodium acetate dissolved in 1000 cm$^3$ of 0.1 M acetic acid. To the above buffer solution, 0.1 mole of sodium acetate is further added and dissolved. The pH of the resulting buffer is ..............
questions.explanation: Initially moles acetate = moles acid = 0.1 (pH=$pK_a$); after adding 0.1 more mole of acetate, [salt]/[acid]=0.2/0.1=2, so pH=$pK_a+\log2$ by the Henderson-Hasselbalch equation.

questions.q: $H_2S$ is passed into one dm$^3$ of a solution containing 0.1 mole of $Zn^{2+}$ and 0.01 mole of $Cu^{2+}$ till the sulphide ion concentration reaches $8.1\times10^{-19}$ moles. Which one of the following statements is true? [$K_{sp}$ of $ZnS$ and $CuS$ are $3\times10^{-22}$ and $8\times10^{-36}$ respectively]
questions.explanation: $Q_{ZnS}=0.1\times8.1\times10^{-19}=8.1\times10^{-20}>K_{sp}(ZnS)$ and $Q_{CuS}=0.01\times8.1\times10^{-19}=8.1\times10^{-21}\gg K_{sp}(CuS)$, so both salts exceed their $K_{sp}$ and precipitate.

questions.q:
$E_1$, $E_2$ and $E_3$ are the emfs of the following three galvanic cells respectively:
(i) $Zn(s)|Zn^{2+}(0.1M)||Cu^{2+}(1M)|Cu(s)$
(ii) $Zn(s)|Zn^{2+}(1M)||Cu^{2+}(1M)|Cu(s)$
(iii) $Zn(s)|Zn^{2+}(1M)||Cu^{2+}(0.1M)|Cu(s)$
Which one of the following is true?
questions.explanation: By the Nernst equation $E=E^0-\dfrac{0.0591}{2}\log\dfrac{[Zn^{2+}]}{[Cu^{2+}]}$, cell (i) has the smallest ratio giving the highest emf and cell (iii) has the largest ratio giving the lowest emf, so $E_1>E_2>E_3$.

questions.q: 0.023 g of sodium metal is reacted with 100 cm$^3$ of water. The pH of the resulting solution is ..............
The standard emf of a galvanic cell involving 2 moles of electrons in its redox reaction is 0.59 V. The equilibrium constant for the redox reaction of the cell is ..............

9.65 coulombs of electric current is passed through fused anhydrous $MgCl_2$. The magnesium metal thus obtained is completely converted into a Grignard reagent. The number of moles of Grignard reagent obtained is ..............
questions.explanation: Moles $e^-$=9.65/96500=$10^{-4}$; $Mg^{2+}+2e^-\to Mg$ gives moles $Mg$=$5\times10^{-5}$, which is fully converted into an equal number of moles of Grignard reagent.

questions.q: The empirical formula of a nonelectrolyte is $CH_2O$. A solution containing 3 g of the compound exerts the same osmotic pressure as that of 0.05 M glucose solution. The molecular formula of the compound is..................
questions.explanation: Equal osmotic pressure implies equal molarity (0.05 M); molar mass = 3 g / 0.05 mol = 60 g/mol = 2×(empirical formula mass 30), giving the molecular formula $C_2H_4O_2$.

questions.q: Which one of the following is a covalent crystal?
questions.explanation: Quartz ($SiO_2$) is a covalent network crystal; rock salt is ionic, while ice and dry ice are molecular crystals held by hydrogen bonds or van der Waals forces.

questions.q: Which one of the following DOES NOT involve coagulation?
options: Clotting of blood by the use of ferric chloride
Treatment of drinking water by potash alum
questions.explanation: Peptization converts a freshly precipitated solid into a colloidal sol, the reverse of coagulation; the other three processes all involve coagulation of colloids by electrolytes.

questions.q: A solution of two liquids boils at a temperature more than the boiling point of either of them. Hence, the binary solution shows ..............
options: positive or negative deviation from Raoult's law depending upon the composition
questions.explanation: A solution boiling higher than either pure component has a lower vapour pressure than expected from stronger unlike-molecule interactions, which is a negative deviation from Raoult's law.

questions.q: Which one of the nitrogen atoms in $H_2N-NH-CO-NH_2$ (labelled I, II, III from left to right) is the most nucleophilic?
options: All three nitrogen atoms are equally strong nucleophilic centers
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry: Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.explanation: Nitrogen I (the terminal $NH_2$ not directly attached to the carbonyl carbon) is not involved in resonance with the $C=O$ group, so its lone pair is fully available, making it the most nucleophilic; nitrogens II and III lose electron density to the carbonyl by resonance.

questions.q: The maximum number of possible optical isomers in 1-bromo-2-methyl cyclobutane is ...
questions.explanation: The molecule has two stereocentres (C1 bearing Br and C2 bearing methyl) with no symmetry in the ring, giving $2^2=4$ stereoisomers (two pairs of enantiomers, cis and trans).

questions.q: Which one of the following is the most energetic conformation of cyclohexane?
questions.explanation: The stability order is chair < twist-boat < boat < half-chair, so the half-chair conformation has the highest energy.

questions.q: Which one of the following is an intermediate in the reaction of benzene with $CH_3Cl$ in the presence of anhydrous $AlCl_3$?
options: the arenium (cyclohexadienyl) cation formed by attack of the electrophile on the benzene ring
questions.explanation: $AlCl_3$ abstracts $Cl^-$ from $CH_3Cl$ to generate the electrophile $CH_3^+$ (as an $AlCl_4^-$ complex), which then attacks benzene.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT TRUE for the hydrolysis of $t$-butyl bromide with aqueous $NaOH$?
options: The intermediate formed is a carbocation.
Rate of the reaction doubles when the concentration of alkali is doubled.
Rate of the reaction doubles when the concentration of $t$-butyl bromide is doubled.
questions.explanation: The reaction proceeds by $S_N1$, so its rate depends only on the substrate concentration, not on $[OH^-]$; hence doubling the alkali concentration does not double the rate.

questions.q:
Following is the substitution reaction in which $-CN$ replaces $-Cl$.
$R-Cl+KCN\xrightarrow[\text{(alcoholic)}]{\Delta}R-CN+KCl$
To obtain propanenitrile, $R-Cl$ should be ..................
questions.explanation: Propanenitrile is $CH_3CH_2CN$ (3 carbons including the nitrile carbon), so $R=C_2H_5$, meaning $R-Cl$ is chloroethane.

questions.q: The conversion of $m$-nitrophenol to resorcinol involves respectively ..................
questions.explanation: $m$-Nitrophenol is first reduced to $m$-aminophenol, then diazotized to the diazonium salt, which is finally hydrolyzed to give resorcinol.

questions.q: Formic acid is a stronger acid than acetic acid. This can be explained using ..........
questions.explanation: The methyl group in acetic acid exerts a +I (electron-donating) effect that destabilizes its conjugate base, making acetic acid weaker than formic acid, which lacks this alkyl group.

questions.q: The reagent with which both acetaldehyde and acetone react is ..............
questions.explanation: Both acetaldehyde and acetone contain a $CH_3CO-$ group and give a positive iodoform test with $I_2/NaOH$; Fehling's and Tollens' reagents react only with aldehydes, not ketones.

questions.q: Which of the following gives an aldehyde on dry distillation?
questions.explanation: Dry distillation of a mixture of calcium formate and calcium acetate gives acetaldehyde ($CH_3CHO$) along with calcium carbonate.

questions.q: $\alpha$-maltose consists of ..................
options: one $\alpha$-D-glucopyranose unit and one $\beta$-D-glucopyranose unit with 1-2 glycosidic linkage
questions.explanation: Maltose is formed from two $\alpha$-D-glucopyranose units joined by a $1\to4$ glycosidic linkage.

questions.q: Which one of the following DOES NOT correctly match with each other?
questions.explanation: Oxytocin is a peptide hormone, not an enzyme, so this pairing is incorrect; silk-polyamide, lipase-enzyme and butter-fat are all correct pairings.

questions.q: In an alkaline medium, glycine predominantly exists as/in a/an ..................
questions.explanation: In alkaline medium, the carboxyl group of glycine is deprotonated while the amino group stays unprotonated, so it exists predominantly as the anion.

questions.q: The IUPAC name of $CH_2{=}CH-CH_2-COOH$ is ..............
questions.explanation: Numbering from the carboxylic acid carbon (C1) gives $CH_2{=}CH-CH_2-COOH$ as but-3-enoic acid, with the double bond between C3 and C4.
